DS.name: Disposition
DS.structure: One record per disposition status or protocol milestone per subject
DS.purpose: Accounts for every subject who entered the study — protocol milestones (e.g. consent, randomization/enrollment) and completion/discontinuation status for the whole study or each phase/segment (screening, treatment, follow-up).
DS.construction: DS is a MULTI-SOURCE MERGE, not a single-form copy. Each subject contributes several DS records, one per disposition/milestone event, drawn from different source forms (informed consent, enrollment/screening, study-drug completion/discontinuation, study completion/discontinuation, death, visit/epoch dates). Build it per source event: (1) USUBJID from the subject key; (2) DSSTDTC = the event date in ISO 8601 — a SINGLE date, DS events never span an interval so there is NO end date; (3) DSCAT = DISPOSITION EVENT / PROTOCOL MILESTONE / OTHER EVENT for that source; (4) DSDECOD from the controlled terminology that matches DSCAT; (5) DSTERM = the original/verbatim value (upper-cased), or the same value as DSDECOD for milestones with no separate reason. Then STACK all source events into one dataset, number DSSEQ within USUBJID, derive DSDY from DSSTDTC vs DM.RFSTDTC (no day 0), and set EPOCH from the event's timing. Extra reported reasons go to SUPPDS (DSTERM1/DSDECOD1).
rules: DSCAT categorizes the record: 'DISPOSITION EVENT' (completion/discontinuation), 'PROTOCOL MILESTONE' (consent, randomization, enrollment, entered-into-trial), or 'OTHER EVENT'.
DSDECOD controlled terminology DEPENDS ON DSCAT: DISPOSITION EVENT→codelist NCOMPLT; PROTOCOL MILESTONE→codelist PROTMLST; OTHER EVENT→sponsor terminology.
DISPOSITION EVENT: DSTERM='COMPLETED' → DSDECOD='COMPLETED'; else DSTERM=verbatim reason and DSDECOD=its coded term (e.g. 'Subject moved' → 'LOST TO FOLLOW-UP').
PROTOCOL MILESTONE: DSTERM = milestone name (verbatim/standardized); DSDECOD same or standardized.
OTHER EVENT: if a reason was collected, DSTERM=reason, DSDECOD=sponsor term; if not, DSTERM=DSDECOD.
Timing: DSSTDTC is expected and is the event date/time; DS records have no --ENDTC.
Do NOT use these Events qualifiers in DS: --PRESP, --OCCUR, --STAT, --REASND, --BODSYS, --LOC, --SEV, --SER, --ACN, --REL, --OUT, --CONTRT, --TOXGR, etc.

DM.name: Demographics
DM.purpose: The parent domain for all other observations — one row per subject with the essential standard variables describing each subject and the subject-level reference dates that drive --DY derivations everywhere else.
DM.construction: DM has EXACTLY ONE record per subject. Assemble it from the enrollment/demographics form plus derived reference dates. Identifiers: USUBJID unique across all studies, SUBJID within the study, SITEID always present (INVID/INVNAM as needed). Collected demographics: AGE/AGEU, SEX, RACE, ETHNIC, COUNTRY, and BRTHDTC (privacy-sensitive; include only if the sponsor submits it). Arm assignment: ARM/ARMCD (planned) and ACTARM/ACTARMCD (actual) come from the Trial Arms (TA) dataset with a preserved one-to-one ARM↔ARMCD relationship; when a subject has no arm, those are null and ARMNRS carries the coded reason (e.g. 'SCREEN FAILURE', 'NOT ASSIGNED'). The subject reference dates are DERIVED, not collected: RFXSTDTC = earliest EXSTDTC, RFXENDTC = latest EXENDTC (or latest EXSTDTC if EXENDTC missing), RFSTDTC usually = first study-treatment date (drives every domain's --DY), RFENDTC = trial end (null for screen failures / unassigned), RFICDTC = informed-consent date, RFPENDTC = participation end. DTHDTC/DTHFL from the death form.
rules: Only ONE DM record per subject; USUBJID must be unique across all studies for the product.
RFXSTDTC = earliest EXSTDTC across the subject's exposure; RFXENDTC = latest EXENDTC (or latest EXSTDTC when EXENDTC not collected).
RFSTDTC = subject reference start (usually first exposure) — it is the anchor for all --DY. RFENDTC required for randomized subjects; null for screen failures / unassigned subjects.
ARM & ARMCD must be TA values with the one-to-one relationship preserved; ACTARM/ACTARMCD likewise; when null, ARMNRS gives the coded reason.
SITEID is always present; use INVID/INVNAM as needed and document the convention in Define-XML.
BRTHDTC is privacy-sensitive — include only per regulatory guidance.

variables.label: Subject Identifier for the Study
variables.cdisc_note: Subject identifier, which must be unique within the study. Often the ID of the subject as recorded on a CRF.

variables.label: Subject Reference Start Date/Time
variables.cdisc_note: Reference start date/time for the subject in ISO 8601 character format. Usually equivalent to date/time when subject was first exposed to study treatment. See assumption 9 for additional detail on when RFSTDTC may be null.

variables.label: Subject Reference End Date/Time
variables.cdisc_note: Reference end date/time for the subject in ISO 8601 character format. Usually equivalent to the date/time when subject was determined to have ended the trial, and often equivalent to date/time of last exposure to study treatment. Required for all randomized subjects; null for screen failures or unassigned subjects.

variables.label: Date/Time of First Study Treatment
variables.cdisc_note: First date/time of exposure to any protocol-specified treatment or therapy, equal to the earliest value of EXSTDTC.

variables.label: Date/Time of Last Study Treatment
variables.cdisc_note: Last date/time of exposure to any protocol-specified treatment or therapy, equal to the latest value of EXENDTC (or the latest value of EXSTDTC if EXENDTC was not collected or is missing).

variables.label: Date/Time of First Challenge Agent Admin
variables.cdisc_note: Used only when protocol specifies a challenge agent to induce a condition that the investigational treatment is intended to cure, mitigate, treat, or prevent. Equal to the earliest value of AGSTDTC for the challenge agent.

variables.label: Date/Time of Last Challenge Agent Admin
variables.cdisc_note: Used only when protocol specifies a challenge agent to induce a condition that the investigational treatment is intended to cure, mitigate, treat, or prevent. Equal to the latest value of AGENDTC for the challenge agent (or the latest value of AGSTDTC if AGENDTC was not collected or is missing).

variables.label: Date/Time of Informed Consent
variables.cdisc_note: Date/time of informed consent in ISO 8601 character format. This will be the same as the date of informed consent in the Disposition domain, if that protocol milestone is documented. Would be null only in studies not collecting the date of informed consent.

variables.label: Date/Time of End of Participation
variables.cdisc_note: Date/time when subject ended participation or follow-up in a trial, as defined in the protocol, in ISO 8601 character format. Should correspond to the last known date of contact. Examples include completion date, withdrawal date, last follow-up, date recorded for lost to follow up, and death date.

variables.label: Date/Time of Death
variables.cdisc_note: Date/time of death for any subject who died, in ISO 8601 format. Should represent the date/time that is captured in the clinical-trial database.

variables.label: Subject Death Flag
variables.cdisc_note: Indicates the subject died. Should be "Y" or null. Should be populated even when the death date is unknown.

variables.label: Study Site Identifier
variables.cdisc_note: Unique identifier for a site within a study.

variables.label: Investigator Identifier
variables.cdisc_note: An identifier to describe the Investigator for the study. May be used in addition to SITEID. Not needed if SITEID is equivalent to INVID.

variables.label: Investigator Name

variables.label: Planned Arm Code
variables.cdisc_note: ARMCD is limited to 20 characters. It is not subject to the character restrictions that apply to TESTCD. The maximum length of ARMCD is longer than for other "short" variables to accommodate the kind of values that are likely to be needed for crossover trials. For example, if ARMCD values for a 7-period crossover were constructed using 2-character abbreviations for each treatment and separating hyphens, the length of ARMCD values would be 20. If the subject was not assigned to a trial arm, ARMCD is null and ARMNRS is populated. \n With the exception of studies which use multistage arm assignments, must be a value of ARMCD in the Trial Arms dataset.

variables.label: Description of Planned Arm
variables.cdisc_note: Name of the arm to which the subject was assigned. If the subject was not assigned to an arm, ARM is null and ARMNRS is populated. \n With the exception of studies which use multistage arm assignments, must be a value of ARM in the Trial Arms dataset.

variables.label: Actual Arm Code
variables.cdisc_note: Code of actual arm. ACTARMCD is limited to 20 characters. It is not subject to the character restrictions that apply to TESTCD. The maximum length of ACTARMCD is longer than for other short variables to accommodate the kind of values that are likely to be needed for crossover trials. \n With the exception of studies which use multistage arm assignments, must be a value of ARMCD in the Trial Arms dataset. \n If the subject was not assigned to an arm or followed a course not described by any planned arm, ACTARMCD is null and ARMNRS is populated.

variables.label: Description of Actual Arm
variables.cdisc_note: Description of actual arm. \n With the exception of studies which use multistage arm assignments, must be a value of ARM in the Trial Arms dataset. \n If the subject was not assigned to an arm or followed a course not described by any planned arm, ACTARM is null and ARMNRS is populated.

variables.label: Reason Arm and/or Actual Arm is Null
variables.cdisc_note: A coded reason that arm variables (ARM and ARMCD) and/or actual arm variables (ACTARM and ACTARMCD) are null. Examples: "SCREEN FAILURE", "NOT ASSIGNED", "ASSIGNED, NOT TREATED", "UNPLANNED TREATMENT". It is assumed that if the arm and actual arm variables are null, the same reason applies to both arm and actual arm.

variables.label: Description of Unplanned Actual Arm
variables.cdisc_note: A description of actual treatment for a subject who did not receive treatment described in a planned trial arm.

variables.label: Country
variables.cdisc_note: Country of the investigational site in which the subject participated in the trial. \n \n Generally represented using ISO 3166-1 Alpha-3. Note that regulatory agency specific requirements (e.g., US FDA) may require other terminologies; in such cases, follow regulatory requirements.

variables.label: Date/Time of Collection
variables.cdisc_note: Date/time of demographic data collection.

variables.label: Study Day of Collection
variables.cdisc_note: Study day of collection measured as integer days.
